answer: A concrete Sybil defense is proof-of-work gated identity: each new host must solve a hash puzzle whose difficulty rises with how many identities already share its funding source or IP prefix. Every extra identity therefore costs roughly double the last, so farming ten thousand fake hosts burns real electricity instead of being free. The challenge cipher forces sequential compute that cannot be outsourced cheaply, and older verified hosts act as an anchor that sybils cannot buy, so a farm stays an empty haven with no stake and pays more in energy than it can capture.
